revisions.evidence_base_difference: cb428270 differs from 212f8442 only by previously committed checker evidence.

results.failure_summary: Java measures the label at textLength 185.7324; Rust measures 181.5391. The narrower Rust label box changes the routed path and target x position and produces a 494px canvas instead of Java's 498px canvas.

findings.finding: The complete-face change is generative for printable ASCII but not for valid Unicode labels. times_new_roman_text_width uses the selected face table only for codepoints 32 through 126 and assigns every other glyph a fixed 1024-unit half-em advance. Java AWT measures the real Times New Roman glyph advances. Accented Latin letters and an em dash therefore produce a 4.1933px label-width error at size 19, which propagates through Graphviz into route, node position, and canvas differences.
findings.scope_assessment: The account places no ASCII-only restriction on transition labels, and Java accepts and renders this valid PlantUML input. The failure affects the claimed transition-label measurement and painted-envelope mechanism directly, so it is in scope.

findings.finding: The original three counterexamples and eight new printable-ASCII controls pass. Font ownership, canonical dotted/underscored key identity, all four Times ASCII faces, configured/natural alignment, and ordinary/self painted envelopes are supported by the evidence.

One original failing phrase remains in a unit assertion, but production code contains no fixture-label branch. Because the independently generated Unicode case fails through the general fallback, the checker did not mistake the complete ASCII table for a complete glyph model.

verdict_reason: A fresh valid in-scope Times New Roman transition label fails the supplied no-oracle comparator. T14's held-out perturbation rule requires any such counterexample to reject the change and remain executable, regardless of the eight new passing controls and the repaired original nine cases.
